To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
thiophenyl benzofurans are a new class of potent and selective P-gp inhibitors.
thiophenyl-2,3-dihydro-1-benzofuranyl (THBF) derivatives were designed and synthesized as novel P-gp inhibitors.
thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives (1-31) were designed, synthesized and evaluated for their ability to inhibit P-gp, and compounds 4,10 and 14 were identified as the most promising P-gp inhibitors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of thiophenolbenzofuran analogs as P-gp modulators.
the synthesis of thiophenylethylbenzofurans as potential MDR-reversing agents.
the design and synthesis of novel thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives as a novel class of P-gp inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthesized compounds 4,10, and 13 are promising MDR-reversing agents for further development.
thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives are promising candidates to overcome MDR in cancer chemotherapy.
thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives (especially compounds 4,10,14) may represent potential P-gp inhibitors with therapeutic value in reversing the MDT phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiophenyl group is a critical structural element in the thiophenylethynylbenzofurans (4, 10), and the thiophenylene group is also important in thiophenylphenylethynyl derivatives (14, 21).
thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives are promising MDR-reversing agents for further investigation.
thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives (1-31) were identified as potential P-gp inhibitors for reversing MDR in human cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives are promising MDR-reversing agents, and that these agents are worthy of further development for cancer therapy.
the thiophenyl group is a key pharmacophore in thiophenyl benzofuran derivatives for the inhibition of P-gp activity and MDR phenotype reversal.
these compounds may serve as promising leads in the development of new P-gp modulators.
